brief.title: Usage-based Billing & Invoicing Platform
business_goals: Enable usage-based pricing per API call
Eliminate manual spreadsheet reconciliation for usage
Provide customers with real-time visibility into their API usage
Ensure accurate calculation of tiered charges for revenue recognition
Ensure timely generation and sending of invoices (within 24 hours of period close)
Prevent billing disputes due to undercounted usage by handling high volume metering events without loss
Automate dunning and failed-payment retry logic
Reduce internal 'fire drills' and discrepancies related to billing numbers

stakeholders.name: Laura Bennett
concerns: Scalability of billing operations beyond 400 customers
Accurate calculation of tiered pricing for revenue recognition
Timely invoice generation (within 24 hours of period close)
Seven years of invoice and usage data retention for tax and audit purposes

stakeholders.name: Chris Nakamura
concerns: Customers need real-time visibility into their usage (updated within minutes)
Customers need usage alerts (e.g., 80% of spending cap via email)

stakeholders.name: Omar Haddad
concerns: Billing system must consume metering events from existing Kafka topic (from Kong API gateway)
Metering pipeline must handle high volume (40 million API calls/month for largest customer) without dropping events
Avoiding billing disputes due to undercounted usage
Reducing internal 'Slack fire drills' caused by billing discrepancies

stakeholders.name: Grace Lindqvist
concerns: Invoices must be sent through Stripe (existing payment processor)
Automated dunning and failed-payment retry logic (e.g., retry three times over a week)

constraints: Current spreadsheet reconciliation process does not scale past 400 customers
Billing system must consume usage events from an existing Kafka topic
Must support tiered pricing (e.g., first 100,000 calls at one rate, above at lower rate)
Must integrate with Stripe as the existing payment processor; no switching payment processors
Invoices must be generated and sent within 24 hours of the billing period closing
Metering pipeline must handle 40 million API calls/month for largest customer without dropping events
Seven years of invoice and usage data must be retained for tax and audit purposes
System must be live before fiscal year starts on July 1st
Project budget is capped at $400,000 (including Kafka and Stripe integration)
out_of_scope: Multi-currency billing for this phase (only USD invoicing)
open_questions: What is the acceptable latency for 'real-time visibility' into customer usage (e.g., within 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes)?
How do customers set spending caps for usage alerts? Is this a new feature or an existing one?
What are the exact retry intervals and notification mechanisms for automated dunning and failed payments?

requirements.statement: The system shall provide customers with visibility into their API calls consumed within the current billing period.
requirements.evidence: Customers need real-time visibility into their own usage — API calls consumed so far this billing period, ideally updated within a few minutes, not just at month end.
assumptions: "Real-time visibility" means usage data is updated within a few minutes, pending clarification from open questions.

requirements.statement: The system shall consume metering events from the existing Kafka topic.
requirements.evidence: the billing system needs to consume from that topic rather than us building a second metering layer.

requirements.statement: The system shall calculate tiered charges based on customer-specific contracted rates and usage thresholds.
requirements.rationale: Incorrect calculation directly impacts revenue recognition.
requirements.evidence: The system has to calculate tiered charges correctly, we cannot get this wrong, it directly hits revenue recognition.

requirements.statement: The system shall send email notifications to customers when their usage reaches 80% of a predefined spending cap.
requirements.evidence: We also want usage alerts — ideally customers get notified by email when they hit 80% of any spending cap they've set for themselves.
assumptions: Customers can set their own spending caps, pending clarification from open questions.

requirements.statement: The system shall send invoices through Stripe.
requirements.rationale: Stripe is the existing payment processor with customer cards on file.
requirements.evidence: Invoices need to go out through Stripe, since that's our existing payment processor and customers already have cards on file there — we are not switching payment processors as part of this.

requirements.statement: The system shall generate and send invoices within 24 hours of the billing period closing.
requirements.rationale: To prevent customer escalations due to late invoices.
requirements.evidence: Invoices must be generated and sent within 24 hours of the billing period closing.

requirements.statement: The system shall process 40 million API calls per month for a single customer without dropping metering events.
requirements.rationale: To prevent billing disputes due to undercounted usage.
requirements.evidence: The metering pipeline needs to handle that volume without dropping events — we can't have billing disputes because we undercounted someone's usage.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically retry failed payments three times over a one-week period before flagging the account for manual review.
requirements.evidence: Dunning and failed-payment retry logic should ideally be automatic — retry a failed card three times over a week before flagging the account to a human.
assumptions: The exact retry intervals within the one-week period are to be defined, pending clarification from open questions.

requirements.statement: The system shall retain seven years of invoice and usage data.
requirements.rationale: Required for tax and audit purposes.
requirements.evidence: We need seven years of invoice and usage data retained for tax and audit purposes, that's a hard finance requirement, not optional.

epics.title: Real-time Usage Monitoring
epics.goal: Provide customers with immediate visibility into their API usage and proactive notifications to manage their spending.

epics.title: Robust Metering & Data Ingestion
epics.goal: Ensure all API usage data is reliably captured and processed at high volumes without loss for accurate billing.

epics.title: Accurate Billing & Invoicing
epics.goal: Automate the calculation of charges, timely generation of invoices, and long-term retention of billing data.

epics.title: Automated Payment Processing
epics.goal: Streamline the delivery of invoices and automate the recovery of failed payments to minimize manual intervention.

stories.title: Customer Usage Visibility
stories.i_want: to view my API calls consumed within the current billing period
stories.so_that: I can understand my current usage and potential charges

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged into my customer portal
acceptance_criteria.when: I navigate to the 'Usage' section
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard displays my API calls consumed in the current billing period

acceptance_criteria.given: I have not made any API calls in the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.when: I view my usage details
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays '0' API calls consumed

acceptance_criteria.given: I have made 1,234,567 API calls in the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.when: I view my usage details
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays '1,234,567' API calls consumed

stories.title: Kafka Metering Event Ingestion
stories.i_want: to ingest metering events from the existing Kafka topic
stories.so_that: I can ensure the integrity of billing data

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid metering event is published to the Kafka topic
acceptance_criteria.when: the system consumes the event
acceptance_criteria.then: the event data is stored in the usage database

acceptance_criteria.given: a malformed metering event is published to the Kafka topic
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to consume the event
acceptance_criteria.then: the event is logged as an error and not processed for billing

acceptance_criteria.given: the Kafka topic is temporarily unavailable
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to consume events
acceptance_criteria.then: the system logs the connection failure and pauses event consumption, then attempts to reconnect after a defined interval

stories.title: Tiered Charge Calculation
stories.i_want: the system to calculate tiered charges based on customer-specific contracted rates and usage thresholds
stories.so_that: invoices reflect the correct amount based on their contract

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has a contract with a single tier rate of $0.01 per API call
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates charges for 1,000 API calls
acceptance_criteria.then: the total charge is $10.00

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has a contract with two tiers: $0.01 for the first 1000 calls, $0.005 for calls above 1000
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates charges for 1,500 API calls

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has a contract with a tier threshold at exactly 1000 calls
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates charges for 1000 API calls
acceptance_criteria.then: the charge for the first tier is applied to all 1000 calls

stories.title: Usage Cap Notification
stories.i_want: to receive an email notification when my usage reaches 80% of a predefined spending cap
stories.so_that: I can manage my API consumption and avoid unexpected overages

acceptance_criteria.given: my spending cap is $1000 and my current usage reaches $800
acceptance_criteria.when: the system detects the threshold has been met
acceptance_criteria.then: an email notification is sent to my registered email address

acceptance_criteria.given: my spending cap is $1000 and my current usage is $799
acceptance_criteria.when: the system checks my usage
acceptance_criteria.then: no email notification is sent

acceptance_criteria.given: my spending cap is $1000 and my current usage jumps from $750 to $850 in one event
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the usage update
acceptance_criteria.then: a single email notification is sent to my registered email address

stories.title: Stripe Invoice Sending
stories.i_want: to send generated invoices through Stripe
stories.so_that: invoices are delivered promptly and payment collection is initiated

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid invoice has been generated for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to send the invoice to Stripe
acceptance_criteria.then: the system receives a successful API response from Stripe, including a Stripe invoice ID, and updates the invoice status to 'Sent' in the billing system

acceptance_criteria.given: Stripe's API is temporarily unavailable
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to send an invoice
acceptance_criteria.then: the system schedules a retry for sending the invoice and logs the API error

acceptance_criteria.given: an invoice fails validation by Stripe (e.g., invalid customer ID)
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to send the invoice
acceptance_criteria.then: the invoice is flagged for manual review and an error is logged

stories.title: Automated Invoice Generation and Sending
stories.i_want: the system to automatically generate and send invoices
stories.so_that: all customers receive their invoices promptly after the billing period closes

acceptance_criteria.given: the billing period has closed for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the automated invoice process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: a valid invoice is generated and sent via Stripe within 24 hours

acceptance_criteria.given: the billing period has closed for 100 customers
acceptance_criteria.when: the automated invoice process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: all 100 invoices are generated and sent within 24 hours

acceptance_criteria.given: an error occurs during invoice generation for a specific customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the automated invoice process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the error is logged, and other customer invoices continue to be processed

stories.notes: This story depends on S-003 (Tiered Charge Calculation) and S-005 (Stripe Invoice Sending) being completed or well-defined.

stories.title: Baseline High Volume Metering Event Ingestion
stories.i_want: to ingest 40 million API calls per month from a single customer without loss
stories.so_that: all usage data is accurately captured for billing purposes

acceptance_criteria.given: a single customer generates 40 million API calls within a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes these metering events
acceptance_criteria.then: all 40 million events are successfully ingested and stored without loss

acceptance_criteria.given: the system is under high load processing metering events
acceptance_criteria.when: an internal service dependency becomes slow
acceptance_criteria.then: the system continues to ingest all events without loss by buffering or rate-limiting as needed

stories.title: Automated Failed Payment Retries
stories.i_want: the system to automatically retry failed payments three times over a one-week period
stories.so_that: we can recover revenue without manual intervention

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's payment fails for the first time
acceptance_criteria.when: the system detects the failure
acceptance_criteria.then: the system schedules a retry for the payment within 24 hours

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's payment has failed three times over a one-week period
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts the fourth payment retry
acceptance_criteria.then: the account is flagged for manual review and no further automatic retries are scheduled

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's payment fails twice and then succeeds on the third retry
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the successful payment
acceptance_criteria.then: the account is no longer flagged for payment issues and no further retries are scheduled

stories.title: Invoice and Aggregated Usage Data Retention
stories.i_want: to retain invoice and aggregated usage data for seven years
stories.so_that: we meet regulatory compliance and can resolve historical billing disputes

acceptance_criteria.given: an invoice and its associated aggregated usage data are 6 years and 11 months old
acceptance_criteria.when: a query is made for this historical data
acceptance_criteria.then: the invoice and aggregated usage data are successfully retrieved within 5 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: an invoice and its associated aggregated usage data are 7 years and 1 day old
acceptance_criteria.when: a query is made for this historical data
acceptance_criteria.then: the invoice and aggregated usage data are still accessible and retrievable within 5 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: the data retention policy is configured for 7 years
acceptance_criteria.when: an invoice and its associated aggregated usage data reach 7 years of age
acceptance_criteria.then: the invoice and aggregated usage data remain accessible and are not automatically deleted by the system

issues: AC1.then: 'stored in the usage database' is an implementation detail and not an observable outcome for a tester.
AC2.then: 'not processed for billing' is vague. How would a tester verify this outcome?
AC3.then: 'defined interval' is vague. The specific interval and retry mechanism should be specified for testability.
AC3.then has no observable outcome verb
reviews.fix_instructions: Rewrite AC1.then to describe an observable outcome (e.g., 'the event data is available via an internal API for auditing'). Rewrite AC2.then to specify an observable outcome (e.g., 'an alert is triggered for manual review of the malformed event'). Specify the 'defined interval' and retry count in AC3.then.

issues: AC2.then: 'schedules a retry' is vague. The number of retries and the interval between retries should be specified to make it testable and estimable.
reviews.fix_instructions: Specify the number of retries and the interval for scheduling retries in AC2.then. For example, 'the system schedules a retry for sending the invoice within 1 hour, up to 3 times, and logs the API error.'

issues: The story explicitly states dependencies on S-003 and S-005, violating the 'Independent' INVEST principle.
reviews.fix_instructions: This story cannot be truly independent if it orchestrates other stories. Consider if 'Automated Invoice Generation' and 'Automated Invoice Sending' could be separate stories, with this story being an 'Orchestration' story that depends on both. If kept as is, acknowledge the dependency and plan accordingly, but it will always score low on independence.

issues: AC2.then: 'buffering or rate-limiting as needed' is an implementation detail. The focus should be on the observable outcome of 'without loss' under stress.

AC2.then: 'without loss' needs more specific observable criteria under the given conditions. How would a tester verify that no events were lost when an internal service is slow? What are the metrics, alerts, or logs?
The scale (40 million events) and resilience requirements make this a significant effort, potentially too large for a single story.
AC2.then has no observable outcome verb
reviews.fix_instructions: Rewrite AC2.then to remove implementation details like 'buffering or rate-limiting'. Instead, specify observable outcomes for verifying 'without loss' under stress, such as specific monitoring metrics, alerts, or audit logs that confirm event integrity and throughput. Consider breaking this into smaller stories if the implementation of high-volume ingestion and resilience is complex.

issues: AC3.then: 'remains accessible' is somewhat redundant with AC2. The core point of AC3 seems to be the non-deletion aspect, which could be more concisely stated.
reviews.fix_instructions: Refine AC3.then to focus specifically on the non-deletion aspect, perhaps by stating 'the invoice and aggregated usage data are not automatically deleted by the system and remain available for retrieval.'

gaps.description: The business goal to scale billing operations beyond 400 customers is not explicitly covered by a specific requirement or story that defines the system's capacity for the total number of customers or invoices, beyond the metering volume for a single customer.
gaps.suggested_question: What specific metrics (e.g., total customers, invoices per month) define 'scaling billing operations beyond 400 customers' for the new system, and what are the target numbers?

gaps.description: There are no explicit security requirements for the billing system, which will handle sensitive customer usage data and payment information.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the essential security requirements (e.g., data encryption, access controls, audit logging) for a system handling customer billing and payment data?

gaps.description: There are no explicit availability requirements (e.g., uptime targets) for this critical billing and invoicing platform.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the expected uptime and disaster recovery requirements for the billing system, given its critical role in revenue generation?

gaps.description: There are no explicit accessibility requirements for the customer-facing portal (usage visibility, alerts).
gaps.suggested_question: Are there any accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG) that the customer-facing usage portal needs to meet?

gaps.description: Requirement R-001 states 'visibility into their API calls consumed,' but the acceptable latency for 'real-time' updates is not defined.
gaps.suggested_question: What is the acceptable latency for 'real-time visibility' into customer usage (e.g., within 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes)?

gaps.description: Requirement R-004 mentions 'predefined spending cap' for usage alerts, but it's unclear how customers define or manage these caps.
gaps.suggested_question: How will customers set and manage their spending caps for usage alerts? Is this a new feature or an existing one?

gaps.description: Requirement R-008 specifies 'retry failed payments three times over a one-week period,' but the exact retry intervals and customer notification mechanisms are not detailed.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the exact retry intervals for failed payments within the one-week period, and how will customers be notified about these retries?

gaps.description: A billing system handling financial transactions and customer data typically requires input from Legal or Compliance stakeholders, especially regarding data privacy, terms of service, and regulatory adherence beyond just data retention.
gaps.suggested_question: Should we involve a Legal or Compliance stakeholder to review requirements related to data privacy, terms of service, and other regulatory aspects of the billing system?

gaps.description: While Engineering and Customer Success are involved, a dedicated Support or Operations team would typically have specific requirements for monitoring, troubleshooting, and day-to-day management of a critical billing system.
gaps.suggested_question: Who will be responsible for the day-to-day operational support and monitoring of the new billing system, and have their specific needs been captured?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for the core functional requirements of usage-based billing, including metering, tiered pricing, invoice generation, and basic dunning. Key integrations with Kafka and Stripe are also addressed. However, there are significant gaps in non-functional requirements like security and overall system availability, which are critical for a financial platform. Several requirements also lack sufficient detail, leading to ambiguity that could impact implementation and user experience. Finally, important operational and compliance stakeholders appear to be missing from the current list.
